title: Five Forces Rewiring the World: A Spotlight on the Geopolitical Rewiring
description: The integrated global marketplace of the past few decades is giving way to a world organised around trade corridors, capital flows and payment rails redrawn along geopolitical lines, as countries pursue resilience and economic sovereignty over open markets. This session maps where the new corridors are emerging and what is drawing capital and connectivity toward them rather than away. Attendees leave with a clearer sense of which regions and partnerships are worth building around now, ahead of the competition. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Which economic corridors will define the next decade of growth and investment?
description_zh: 過去數十年整合為一體的全球市場，正讓位給一個沿地緣政治界線重新劃定貿易走廊、資本流動與支付軌道的世界——各國把韌性與經濟主權看得比開放市場更重。本場次盤點新走廊正在何處成形，以及是什麼把資本與連結性吸引過去、而非帶離。與會者將更清楚看出，此刻該圍繞哪些區域與夥伴關係提前布局。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：哪些經濟走廊會定義未來十年的成長與投資？

title: Towards New Economic and Financial Corridors
description: New economic corridors, regional payment systems and infrastructure investments are redrawing the map of global capital flows as countries prioritise resilience and sovereignty over open, integrated markets. This panel works through what it actually takes to build trusted cross-border partnerships and interoperable infrastructure inside corridors that are still forming. The discussion leaves the audience with a practical read on which regional alliances and rails are worth committing to now. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Can fintech remain neutral in an increasingly fragmented world?
description_zh: 新的經濟走廊、區域支付系統與基礎建設投資，正重新繪製全球資本流動的版圖——各國把韌性與主權置於開放整合市場之前。本場次探討在這些仍在成形的走廊之中，要建立互信的跨境夥伴關係與可互通的基礎建設，實際上需要什麼。討論將讓聽眾具體判斷，哪些區域聯盟與支付軌道值得現在就投入。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：在日益分裂的世界裡，金融科技還能保持中立嗎？

title: The Single Biggest Social Unrest: Closing the 800m Jobs Gap
description: Governments now face a dual bind: rising unemployment alongside a widening skills shortage that education and training systems are struggling to close fast enough. This panel turns to how reskilling, job redesign and workforce planning can be shared across employers, educators and public institutions rather than left to any one of them. Attendees come away with a sharper view of where responsibility for building an AI-ready workforce actually sits. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: What is the right split of responsibility between employers, universities, governments and multilaterals for closing the skills gap?
description_zh: 各國政府正面臨雙重難題：失業率上升的同時，技能缺口持續擴大，而教育與訓練體系的補位速度遠遠跟不上。本場次聚焦如何讓再培訓、職務再設計與人力規劃由雇主、教育機構與公部門共同承擔，而不是丟給其中任何一方。與會者將更清楚看出，打造具備 AI 能力的勞動力，責任究竟該落在誰身上。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：在弭平技能缺口這件事上，雇主、大學、政府與多邊機構之間合理的責任分工是什麼？

title: The Next Wave of Digital Finance Talent
description: Across financial services, institutions are competing for scarce AI, cybersecurity and data talent while simultaneously reskilling existing staff and redesigning how work gets done. This panel works through what it takes to grow that talent locally, from training pipelines to public-private partnerships, rather than relying on imported expertise. It gives attendees practical models for building capacity that stays where it is built. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: How do you build local capacity rather than importing or offshoring it?
description_zh: 整個金融服務業都在爭搶稀缺的 AI、資安與資料人才，同時還得為既有員工再培訓、重新設計工作方式。本場次探討要在本地培養這些人才需要什麼——從訓練管道到公私協力——而不是仰賴引進外部專才。內容將提供與會者實用的模式，打造留得住的在地能量。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：如何培養在地能量，而不是靠引進人才或委外？

title: Towards New Operating Models in Financial Services
description: Agentic AI is not only changing what work gets done inside a financial institution, it is changing who does it and how decisions get made, with flatter hierarchies and human-and-agent teams already appearing inside the fastest-moving organisations. This panel examines how far institutions can redesign reporting lines and decision rights before the technology outpaces the structure meant to govern it. It leaves the audience with a working view of what the enterprise of 2030 is likely to look like structurally. The tension underneath: operating models built for a pre-agentic institution are running up against decisions that can no longer wait for the organisation chart to catch up.
description_zh: 代理式 AI 改變的不只是金融機構內部「做什麼工作」，還包括「由誰來做」與「決策如何形成」——在腳步最快的組織裡，扁平化的層級與人機協作團隊已經出現。本場次檢視機構能把匯報線與決策權重新設計到什麼程度，才不會讓技術跑在管理結構之前。討論將讓聽眾對 2030 年的企業在組織結構上長什麼樣子，形成可操作的判斷。底層的張力在於：為「前代理式」機構設計的營運模式，正撞上一批無法再等組織圖追上的決策。

title: Building Human Experiences with AI
description: As agentic AI moves from pilot into real credit decisions, real money and real customers, institutions are under pressure to make those systems feel trustworthy and human rather than purely efficient. This panel looks at how design, governance and accountability choices shape whether a customer feels served by a system or processed by one. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of where human judgement still needs to sit inside an increasingly automated customer journey. The harder problem sits underneath: designing AI experiences that feel human risks quietly removing the humans from the loop altogether.
description_zh: 當代理式 AI 從試點走進真實的授信決策、真實的資金與真實的客戶，機構面臨的壓力是要讓這些系統令人信賴、有人味，而不只是有效率。本場次探討設計、治理與問責上的選擇，如何決定客戶感受到的是「被服務」還是「被處理」。聽眾將更清楚看出，在日益自動化的客戶旅程中，人的判斷還必須留在哪些環節。更棘手的問題藏在底下：把 AI 體驗設計得像真人，可能會在不知不覺間把真人整個移出流程。

title: Agentic Infrastructure: Core Banking and the Org Chart of Tomorrow
description: Agentic AI has arrived faster than the organisational models built to absorb it, leaving institutions rebuilding core banking workflows and reporting lines at the same time. This session works through how leading financial institutions are sequencing that dual transformation, from credit and compliance workflows to the human-and-agent teams now running them. Attendees leave with a clearer sense of which capability and governance decisions cannot be deferred without stalling both efforts. For most institutions, there is still no playbook for rebuilding core banking workflows and the org chart together, and few are willing to attempt one alone.
description_zh: 代理式 AI 到來的速度，遠快於用來承接它的組織模式，機構因此得同時重建核心銀行流程與匯報線。本場次探討領先的金融機構如何安排這場雙重轉型的先後次序——從授信與法遵流程，到現在負責執行的人機協作團隊。與會者將更清楚看出，哪些能力與治理決策一旦拖延，就會讓兩邊的轉型一起卡住。對多數機構而言，同時重建核心銀行流程與組織圖仍然無例可循，也少有人願意獨自嘗試。

title: Quantum Talent: Framing the Pipeline Problem
description: Quantum computing's promise in finance keeps outrunning the workforce built to deliver it, and the shortage of specialists is turning into the binding constraint on how quickly the technology moves from pilot to production. This session frames where that pipeline breaks down — inside universities, inside employers, and inside the policy choices that shape both — before proposing where responsibility should actually sit. Attendees leave with a shared vocabulary for the problem and a clearer sense of which lever is likeliest to move first. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Who owns solving quantum's talent pipeline problem — universities, employers, or governments?
description_zh: 量子運算在金融領域的前景，持續跑在能實現它的人才隊伍之前，而專才短缺正逐漸成為技術從試點走向量產的最大瓶頸。本場次先釐清這條人才管道在哪裡斷裂——在大學裡、在雇主端，以及在形塑兩者的政策選擇裡——再提出責任究竟該由誰承擔。與會者將取得談論這個問題的共同語彙，並更清楚哪一個槓桿最可能先動起來。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：解決量子人才管道問題，責任在誰身上——大學、雇主，還是政府？

title: The Agentic Enterprise: Who's Accountable When the Machine Decides?
description: Agentic AI has moved from pilots to systems that touch real credit decisions, real client money and real compliance rules, and the institutions getting the governance right this year are setting the ceiling for the next decade. This session examines where accountability sits once an agent, not a person, initiates the action, across risk, audit and reporting lines. Attendees leave with a sharper view of the controls that need to exist before autonomy is extended further. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Who is accountable when an autonomous agent makes a bad call, moves client money, or silently breaks a compliance rule?
description_zh: 代理式 AI 已從試點走向真正觸及授信決策、客戶資金與法遵規則的系統，而今年把治理做對的機構，將決定未來十年的天花板。本場次檢視當發動行動的是代理程式而非人時，問責該落在何處，橫跨風險、稽核與匯報線。與會者將更清楚看出，在進一步擴大自主權之前，必須先存在哪些控制機制。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：當自主代理程式做出錯誤判斷、動用客戶資金，或在無聲無息間違反法遵規則時，該由誰負責？

title: Quantum's Scarce Talent Problem: Why the Pipeline Is the Real Constraint
description: Early results in live trading show quantum computing moving the needle on pricing and risk, yet progress remains hostage to a scarcity of people who can build past the pilot stage. This session separates where hybrid quantum-classical systems are already creating value from the hardware limits a bigger team could not simply out-hire. The audience leaves with a realistic read on what quantum can deliver now and what still waits on talent nobody has hired. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: is quantum's value in finance real yet, or are compute limits and a thin pipeline of production applications still holding it back?
description_zh: 實盤交易的早期成果顯示，量子運算已在定價與風險上帶來實質差異，但進展仍受制於「能把專案帶出試點階段的人太少」。本場次區分出混合量子—古典系統已經創造價值的環節，以及再多找幾個人也解決不了的硬體極限。聽眾將對量子在當下能交付什麼、又有哪些還卡在尚未招募到的人才上，形成務實的判斷。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：量子在金融的價值已經成真了嗎？還是運算極限與稀薄的量產應用管道仍在拖住它？

title: AI & Core Banking: Who Regulates the Algorithm? Core Banking's New Compliance Perimeter
description: Core banking functions such as credit decisions, trade finance, fraud detection and KYC are shifting from pilot demonstrations into live, algorithm-driven workflows, and the institutions pulling ahead are rebuilding these processes end to end rather than adding AI on top of what already exists. This session looks at what that rebuild actually requires: which controls move from human sign-off to automated checkpoints, and where the audit trail needs redesigning rather than retrofitting. The audience leaves with a practical view of what a genuinely rewired core banking stack looks like. The uncomfortable truth underneath it all is that core banking's compliance perimeter was not built for algorithms making the calls.
description_zh: 授信決策、貿易金融、詐欺偵測與 KYC 等核心銀行職能，正從試點展示轉為實際運行、由演算法驅動的工作流程；跑在前面的機構是把這些流程從頭到尾重建，而不是在既有系統上加掛 AI。本場次探討這場重建實際需要什麼：哪些控制點會從人工簽核轉為自動化檢查，以及稽核軌跡在哪些地方必須重新設計、而非事後補強。聽眾將對真正「重新佈線」過的核心銀行架構長什麼樣子，形成務實的認識。而底下那個令人不安的事實是：核心銀行的法遵邊界，從來就不是為「由演算法下判斷」而設計的。

title: Core Banking, Rewired: Learning How Leading Financial Institutions Are Scaling Agentic AI Across the Enterprise
description: Core banking use cases such as credit decisioning, trade finance, fraud detection and compliance monitoring are finally moving out of the demo stage, and the institutions pulling ahead are treating agentic AI as a workflow rebuild rather than a feature launch. This session looks at how leading financial institutions are scaling agentic AI end to end across these functions, including where governance and data foundations have to change first. The audience leaves with a working model for what deployment actually requires beyond the pilot. Too many of these rebuilds stall halfway once the workflow, not just the model, has to change.
description_zh: 授信決策、貿易金融、詐欺偵測與法遵監控等核心銀行應用終於走出展示階段，而跑在前面的機構是把代理式 AI 當成一次流程重建，而不是一項功能上線。本場次探討領先的金融機構如何在這些職能之間端到端地擴大代理式 AI，包括治理與資料基礎必須先做哪些改變。聽眾將取得一套可用的模型，理解在試點之後真正的部署需要什麼。太多這類重建工程會在半路停擺——因為要改的不只是模型，而是整條工作流程。

title: Agentic Commerce's Trust Gap: The Teams Being Built to Close It
description: The infrastructure for AI-initiated payments is already live, but consumer trust has not caught up to what the technology can already do. This session looks at who is actually resourcing that trust gap, and what a dedicated agentic-commerce team looks like when the customer is software rather than a person. Attendees leave with a sharper sense of where that investment is concentrating and where it is still missing. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: consumers still don't trust AI to place an order for them — who is actually going to spend the money to close that gap?
description_zh: AI 發動支付的基礎建設已經上線，但消費者的信任還沒跟上技術當下的能耐。本場次探討究竟是誰在真正投入資源填補這道信任落差，以及當「客戶」是軟體而非真人時，一支專責的代理式商務團隊該長什麼樣子。與會者將更清楚看出這些投資集中在哪裡、又還缺在哪裡。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：消費者仍然不放心讓 AI 代為下單——究竟誰會真的掏錢來補上這道落差？

title: The FI Enterprise of Tomorrow: What Capabilities, Partnerships and Governance Models Are Required to Build Sustainable Competitive Advantage?
description: Flatter hierarchies and human-and-agent teams are already appearing inside the fastest-moving institutions, and the definition of headcount itself is being rewritten before most organisations have decided what replaces it. This session sets out what capabilities, partnerships and governance models a genuinely agentic enterprise needs to build sustainable competitive advantage, rather than a faster version of the old structure. Participants come away with a framework for judging which of their own capability gaps to close first. Few institutions are building those capabilities and governance models before the org chart forces the issue on them.
description_zh: 在腳步最快的機構裡，扁平化的層級與人機協作團隊已經出現，而「人力編制」的定義本身正被改寫——多數組織甚至還沒決定要用什麼取代它。本場次梳理一家真正代理式的企業，需要哪些能力、夥伴關係與治理模式，才能建立可持續的競爭優勢，而不只是把舊結構跑得更快。與會者將帶走一套框架，用來判斷自家哪些能力缺口該先補。真正在組織圖逼上門之前就著手打造這些能力與治理模式的機構，仍屬少數。

title: AI Changing Operating Models: Governing the Agentic Enterprise of Tomorrow
description: Once agents can direct other agents, the org chart itself starts to change shape: hierarchies flatten, headcount gets redefined, and human-and-agent teams become the operating unit rather than the department. This session works through what that redesign means for decision rights, escalation paths and who ultimately owns an outcome when the work is shared between people and systems. Participants come away with a framework for thinking about their own operating model rather than someone else's org chart. What emerges is a genuine gap: institutions are being asked to govern an agentic enterprise before the governance model itself has caught up with what agents can now do.
description_zh: 當代理程式能夠指揮其他代理程式，組織圖本身就開始改變形狀：層級變扁、人力編制被重新定義，人機協作團隊取代部門成為運作單位。本場次梳理這場重新設計對決策權、升級路徑，以及「當工作由人與系統共同完成時，最終由誰為結果負責」意味著什麼。與會者將帶走一套思考自身營運模式的框架，而不是照抄別人的組織圖。從中浮現的是一道真實的落差：機構被要求治理一家代理式企業，而治理模式本身還沒跟上代理程式如今的能耐。

title: Build, Buy, or Keep Sovereign? The Domain-LLM Data Question Regulators Are Asking
description: Underneath every agentic use case sits a harder technical choice: fine-tune a general model, retrieve against it, or build something smaller and sovereign that never lets sensitive data leave the building. This session works through the trade-offs between those approaches and what the build-versus-buy decision made this year locks in for everything built on top of it. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of which architecture fits their own data, risk appetite and regulatory footprint. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: can a bank trust a model it did not build, running on its most sensitive data?
description_zh: 每一個代理式應用底下，都藏著一道更難的技術抉擇：微調通用模型、在其之上做檢索，還是自建一個規模較小、資料永不離開機構的主權模型。本場次梳理這幾條路線的取捨，以及今年做下的自建或外購決定，會為其上所有建設鎖定什麼樣的前提。聽眾將更清楚哪一種架構適合自家的資料、風險胃納與監理範圍。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：銀行能信任一個不是自己打造、卻跑在最敏感資料上的模型嗎？

title: Programmable Money: Money is Becoming Software
description: Digital currencies, tokenised deposits and programmable rails have matured to the point where value can carry its own instructions, conditions and compliance wherever it moves, turning finance from a record-keeping system into one where the rules sit inside the money itself. This session frames what that shift means across payments, trade and capital markets before the sessions that follow dig into each piece. Attendees leave with a shared vocabulary for programmable money and a sense of how far the implications actually reach. Too many institutions are still treating programmable money as a payments upgrade, when it is closer to a new operating system for the balance sheet.
description_zh: 數位貨幣、代幣化存款與可程式化支付軌道已經成熟到讓價值本身可以帶著指令、條件與法遵規則一起移動——金融因此從一套記帳系統，變成規則直接寫在錢裡面的系統。本場次先勾勒這個轉變在支付、貿易與資本市場的意義，後續場次再逐一深入。與會者將取得談論可程式化貨幣的共同語彙，並理解其影響實際延伸到多遠。太多機構仍把可程式化貨幣當成支付系統的升級，但它更接近資產負債表的新作業系統。

title: Stablecoins: From Fringe to Framework: The Lessons Emerging From Programmable Finance Pilots
description: Stablecoins have moved from crypto curiosity to a regulated payment instrument now that federal legislation is in place and licensed issuance is underway in multiple jurisdictions. This session works through the lessons emerging from early programmable-finance pilots and the real choice institutions face: issue, distribute, custody, or watch deposits quietly migrate elsewhere. The audience leaves with a clearer view of where stablecoins sit in their own product and balance-sheet strategy. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: is stablecoin regulation moving fast enough to keep pace with adoption, or is it already behind?
description_zh: 隨著聯邦立法到位、多個司法管轄區開始發放發行執照，穩定幣已從加密貨幣圈的新奇事物，變成受監理的支付工具。本場次梳理早期可程式化金融試點浮現的經驗，以及機構真正要面對的抉擇：自行發行、負責分銷、提供託管，還是眼睜睜看著存款悄悄流向他處。聽眾將更清楚穩定幣在自家產品與資產負債表策略中的定位。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：穩定幣的監理速度跟得上採用速度嗎，還是早就落後了？

title: Real-Time Containment: Framing What Happens When Agents Fail
description: An agent that makes one bad call can touch thousands of accounts before a human notices, and most institutions have never actually rehearsed what stopping that looks like. This short framing session sets up the containment problem: what a kill switch needs to cover, how fast it needs to fire, and who is authorised to pull it. It gives the audience the vocabulary and the stakes before the fuller discussion that follows. The honest starting point is that containing an agent's mistake before it cascades is still mostly theoretical, because most institutions have not tested what containment actually looks like.
description_zh: 一個代理程式的錯誤判斷，可能在人察覺之前就已觸及數千個帳戶，而多數機構其實從未演練過「該怎麼把它停下來」。這場簡短的開場梳理圍堵問題：緊急停止機制要涵蓋什麼、必須多快啟動，以及誰有權按下去。它為後續更完整的討論鋪陳語彙與利害關係。誠實的起點是：要在代理程式的錯誤擴散之前把它圍堵住，目前多半仍停留在理論——因為多數機構根本沒測試過圍堵實際長什麼樣子。

title: When an Agent's Mistake Cascades in Seconds, What Does Real-Time Containment Look Like?
description: When an agent's error is not caught by a human but by another system, the window for stopping it shrinks from days to seconds, and few institutions have built for that timescale. This session moves past the framing to the mechanics: circuit breakers, transaction limits, rollback procedures and monitoring that runs continuously rather than on a schedule. Attendees leave with a working checklist of what real-time containment needs to include before it is tested for real. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: when an agent's mistake cascades across thousands of accounts in seconds, what does real-time containment actually look like?
description_zh: 當代理程式的錯誤不是被人發現、而是被另一套系統發現時，可供制止的時間窗會從數天縮短到數秒，而少有機構是按這個時間尺度打造的。本場次跳過鋪陳，直接談機制：斷路器、交易限額、回滾程序，以及持續運行而非定期執行的監控。與會者將帶走一份可用的檢核清單，列出即時圍堵在真正上場之前必須具備什麼。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：當代理程式的錯誤在數秒內擴散到數千個帳戶，即時圍堵實際上長什麼樣子？

title: RWA & Tokenization: The Balance Sheet Goes On-Chain: Compressing Settlement, Unlocking Collateral Mobility, Reaching New Investors
description: Tokenised Treasuries, funds and credit have grown sharply, and the institutions ahead are tokenising for the compliance and settlement advantage rather than for novelty. This session examines how tokenisation compresses settlement, unlocks collateral mobility and reaches investors the old wrappers could not. Attendees leave with a practical read on which asset classes are ready now and which still need market infrastructure to catch up. The real test is whether institutions are tokenising real-world assets for the compliance win rather than the novelty, so settlement and collateral mobility genuinely improve.
description_zh: 代幣化的國庫券、基金與信貸產品成長迅速，而領先的機構是為了法遵與結算上的優勢而代幣化，不是為了嚐鮮。本場次檢視代幣化如何壓縮結算時間、釋放擔保品的流動性，並觸及舊有架構接不到的投資人。與會者將務實掌握哪些資產類別已經就緒，哪些還要等市場基礎建設跟上。真正的考驗在於：機構代幣化實體資產，是為了法遵上的實質收穫、而非新鮮感，讓結算與擔保品流動性真的變好。

title: Quantum Secure: Framing the Harvest-Now Threat
description: Long before a quantum computer capable of breaking today's encryption exists, adversaries are already copying encrypted financial data with the intention of unlocking it later, which makes the threat present tense rather than theoretical. This short session frames the harvest-now, decrypt-later problem: what is being captured now, what it exposes, and why waiting for the hardware to arrive is already too late as a strategy. It sets up the scale of the migration ahead for the discussion that follows. The problem nobody has fully claimed yet is that today's encrypted financial secrets are already being harvested for a decryption that has no clear owner assigned to fixing it.
description_zh: 在能破解現行加密的量子電腦問世之前很久，對手就已經在複製加密後的金融資料，打算日後再解開——這讓威脅是現在進行式，而非理論假設。這場簡短場次梳理「先擷取、後解密」的問題：現在被擷取的是什麼、會暴露什麼，以及為什麼「等硬體出現再說」作為策略早已太遲。它為後續討論鋪陳這場遷移工程的規模。目前還沒有人真正認領的難題是：今天的加密金融機密已經在被擷取，而該由誰負責修補這件事，還沒有明確歸屬。

title: Quantum Future: The Multiplying, but Constrained, Value of Quantum
description: The first empirical proofs of quantum value have arrived in live trading, and hybrid quantum-classical systems are now being piloted for portfolio optimisation, risk simulation and derivatives pricing. This short opening frames where that value is emerging and what still holds it back, ahead of the deeper conversation that follows. Attendees leave with a realistic sense of where to invest attention now versus later. Quantum's upside keeps multiplying in theory, while limited fault-tolerant compute, high error rates and a thin talent pipeline still constrain what it can deliver in practice.
description_zh: 量子價值的首批實證成果已在實盤交易中出現，混合量子—古典系統正被試用於投組最佳化、風險模擬與衍生品定價。這場簡短的開場梳理價值正在哪裡浮現、又有什麼仍在拖住它，為後續更深入的對談鋪路。與會者將務實判斷此刻該把注意力投向何處、哪些又可以稍後再說。量子的潛在效益在理論上不斷倍增，但有限的容錯運算能力、偏高的錯誤率與稀薄的人才管道，仍限制著它在實務上能交付的東西。

title: Quantum Future: Which Financial Calculations Will Quantum Improve First, and by How Much?
description: Quantum computing's near-term reality in finance is hybrid and experimental, not the sweeping supremacy the term often implies, and the gains so far sit in controlled pilots rather than production systems. This session looks at where quantum is already improving specific calculations, from bond trade-fill prediction to risk analysis, and what a credible roadmap looks like from here. The audience leaves with a sharper sense of which use cases are worth resourcing now rather than waiting on. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: which financial calculations will quantum improve first, and by how much?
description_zh: 量子運算在金融領域的近期現實是混合式且帶有實驗性質的，並非這個詞常給人的「全面超越」印象；目前的成果多半來自受控試點，而非量產系統。本場次探討量子已經在哪些特定運算上帶來改善——從債券成交預測到風險分析——以及從現在起可信的發展路線圖長什麼樣子。聽眾將更清楚哪些應用值得現在就投入資源，而不是繼續觀望。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：量子會先改善哪些金融運算，改善幅度又有多大？

title: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later: Is the Financial Industry Underestimating the Urgency of Post-Quantum Migration?
description: Cryptographic migration timelines in finance are typically measured in years, but the harvest-now threat means the clock actually started the moment encrypted records were first copied for later decryption. This session pressure-tests whether the industry's current pace of post-quantum migration matches the urgency of that threat, covering cryptographic inventory, prioritisation and the standards now available to migrate against. The audience leaves with a realistic sense of how far behind, or ahead, their own institution actually is. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: is the financial industry underestimating the urgency of post-quantum migration, given that today's encrypted records may already be exposed?
description_zh: 金融業的密碼遷移時程通常以「年」為單位，但「先擷取、後解密」的威脅意味著：計時其實在加密紀錄第一次被複製走的那一刻就開始了。本場次檢驗業界目前的後量子遷移步調，是否配得上這個威脅的急迫性，涵蓋密碼資產盤點、優先順序，以及現有可依循的遷移標準。聽眾將務實了解自家機構究竟落後多少、或領先多少。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：考量到今天的加密紀錄可能早已外洩，金融業是不是低估了後量子遷移的急迫性？

title: Who Builds the Bridge Between National Payment Schemes; and Who Owns the Toll?
Who Owns the Moment an Agent Decides to Pay? The New Contest for Checkout
description: A new kind of buyer has arrived in commerce: the AI agent, deciding where money goes before a human ever reaches checkout. This session unpacks the infrastructure already live for agent-initiated payments and where consumer trust still lags behind it. Attendees leave clearer on where the moment of intent is heading for their own merchant relationships. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: if an AI agent decides where to shop and how to pay, does the moment of intent move from the merchant's checkout page to the platform, and what does that do to merchant economics?
description_zh: 商務場景裡出現了一種新的買家：AI 代理程式——在真人抵達結帳頁之前，就先決定錢要花到哪裡。本場次拆解目前已經上線的代理發動支付基礎建設，以及消費者信任還落後在哪裡。與會者將更清楚「意圖發生的那一刻」對自家的商家關係意味著什麼走向。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：如果由 AI 代理程式決定去哪買、怎麼付，意圖成形的那一刻是否就從商家的結帳頁轉移到平台？這對商家的經濟模型又意味著什麼？

title: Banking 4.0
description: The Agentic Bank opens Day 2 by zooming out, geopolitics, energy retooling, dark factories, autonomous transport, before zooming in on the reckoning inside finance. Autonomous banking cannot run on 1960s core systems, fiat rails, or batch payments, it demands infrastructure built for agents that act, not advise. This keynote strips away the interface to unpack what's underneath, architecture, governance, and risk controls. The key question it looks to answer: what actually separates genuine transformation from a rebranded chatbot?
description_zh: 《代理式銀行》以拉遠鏡頭為第二天揭幕——地緣政治、能源結構重整、無人工廠、自動駕駛運輸——再拉近檢視金融業內部的總清算。自主式銀行不可能跑在 1960 年代的核心系統、法幣軌道或批次支付上；它需要的是為「會行動、而不只是給建議」的代理程式所打造的基礎建設。這場主題演講剝開介面，拆解底下的東西：架構、治理與風險控制。它想回答的關鍵問題是：真正的轉型與換了包裝的聊天機器人，差別究竟在哪裡？

title: Policy Implications of Technology Rewiring
description: Regulators are being asked to anticipate emerging technologies before they become systemic, even as innovation in AI, digital assets and tokenisation continues to outpace the frameworks meant to govern it. This session examines where policy is genuinely ahead of the risk and where it is still reacting to technology already in production. It gives the audience a clearer read of which regulatory shifts are coming and how to prepare for them. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Is policy keeping pace with the technology it is meant to govern, or still catching up?
description_zh: 監理機關被要求在新興技術演變成系統性風險之前就預先因應，但 AI、數位資產與代幣化的創新速度，仍持續超前那些用來規範它們的框架。本場次檢視政策在哪些地方確實走在風險之前，又在哪些地方仍在追趕早已上線的技術。內容將讓聽眾更清楚哪些監理變動即將到來、又該如何準備。講者將深入探討的關鍵問題之一：政策跟得上它該規範的技術嗎，還是仍在追趕？

title: The Technological Rewiring: An age of experimentation, risk and new commercial models: Finance and Tech as engine growth
description: Financial institutions are no longer rewarded simply for experimenting with AI, quantum computing and tokenisation. The advantage has shifted to whoever can scale these technologies enterprise-wide first. This discussion maps where genuine competitive advantage is forming across all three, and what governance, talent and infrastructure it takes to move from pilot to production. Attendees leave with a framework for judging which technology bets are worth committing capital and people to now, and a clear answer to the key question shaping this next phase: is the edge still about experimenting with AI, quantum and tokenisation, or about who scales them first.
description_zh: 金融機構已經不會單純因為「有在嘗試」AI、量子運算與代幣化而獲得回報，優勢已經轉向誰能率先把這些技術擴展到全企業。本場討論盤點這三者的真正競爭優勢正在何處成形，以及從試點走到量產需要什麼樣的治理、人才與基礎建設。與會者將帶走一套框架，用來判斷此刻哪些技術賭注值得投入資本與人力，並得到形塑下一階段的關鍵問題的明確答案：優勢還在於嘗試 AI、量子與代幣化，還是在於誰先把它們規模化。

title: The Great Big Financial Systems Upgrade: Towards Agentic Infrastructure and Tech Risks
description: Moving from legacy infrastructure to agentic systems touches core banking, payments and risk management all at once. The scale of that rebuild is itself becoming a source of systemic risk. This panel works through what a credible migration path looks like, including where legacy risk controls break down under autonomous decision-making. The audience leaves better equipped to sequence its own infrastructure upgrade without creating new points of failure along the way. One key question the panel will dive into: can a systems upgrade this large happen without the tech risk it is meant to manage becoming the bigger story.
description_zh: 從既有基礎建設轉向代理式系統，會同時牽動核心銀行、支付與風險管理，而這場重建工程的規模本身，正在變成系統性風險的來源之一。本場次梳理可信的遷移路徑長什麼樣子，包括既有的風險控制在自主決策之下會從哪裡失效。聽眾將更有能力安排自家基礎建設升級的先後次序，而不在過程中製造新的失效點。講者將深入探討的一個關鍵問題：這麼大規模的系統升級，有沒有可能不讓「它本來要管理的科技風險」反而成為更大的話題。

title: Quantum Simulated Solutions: What's Next and How Do We Get There?
description: The first genuine proof points for quantum computing in finance have started to appear in live trading and portfolio optimisation. This is happening even as fault-tolerant compute, talent and production-ready applications all remain scarce. This discussion separates where quantum is already creating measurable value from where enthusiasm is still running ahead of the hardware. It leaves the audience with a realistic sense of where to invest through the hype rather than around it. One key question the discussion will dive into: what does a credible hybrid quantum-classical roadmap actually look like for a bank today, and can it be trusted before fault-tolerant compute arrives.
description_zh: 量子運算在金融領域的首批真實佐證，已經開始出現在實盤交易與投組最佳化上——而這一切發生的同時，容錯運算能力、人才與可量產的應用卻依然稀缺。本場討論區分出量子已經創造可衡量價值的環節，以及熱情仍跑在硬體之前的部分，讓聽眾務實判斷該如何穿過炒作、而不是繞著炒作投資。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：對今天的銀行而言，可信的混合量子—古典路線圖究竟長什麼樣子？在容錯運算問世之前，它可以被信任嗎？

title: Programmable Money: The Value of Money Becoming Software
description: Stablecoins, tokenised deposits and programmable rails have matured from pilot to policy. Value can now move with its own conditions attached, built directly into the money itself. This marks a shift from finance as a system that records transactions after the fact to one where the rules are embedded upfront. This discussion explores what that means for trade, capital markets and public finance, beyond the payments use cases already getting attention. Audiences leave with a clearer view of who ends up writing the rules embedded in tomorrow's money. Most institutions are still building the framework to catch up with a fact that has already arrived: money is starting to carry its own conditions.
description_zh: 穩定幣、代幣化存款與可程式化支付軌道已經從試點走進政策。價值現在可以帶著自己的條件一起移動，而這些條件直接內建在錢裡面。這標誌著金融從「事後記錄交易的系統」，轉向「規則預先嵌入其中的系統」。本場討論探討這對貿易、資本市場與公共財政意味著什麼——超出目前已經受到關注的支付應用。聽眾將更清楚，最終是誰在書寫未來貨幣裡所嵌入的規則。多數機構仍在建立框架，追趕一個早已成真的事實：錢，開始帶著自己的條件了。

title: Future of Money
description: Recognition as money is no longer a settled question. Bank deposits, stablecoins and tokenised assets are all now competing to be treated as trusted, spendable money on institutional balance sheets. This closing discussion pulls together the threads on programmable money from across the festival into a single view of where the category is heading. It sends the audience away with a sharper sense of which form of money is likely to win institutional trust first. The unresolved question at the heart of it: when banks, regulators and businesses can choose between deposits, stablecoins and tokenised assets, which one actually becomes "real money" first.
description_zh: 什麼算是「錢」，已不再是個定論。銀行存款、穩定幣與代幣化資產，如今都在爭取被機構的資產負債表視為可信、可支付的貨幣。這場閉幕討論把整個活動中關於可程式化貨幣的線索收攏成單一視角，勾勒這個類別的走向，讓聽眾更清楚哪一種形態的貨幣可能率先贏得機構信任。核心的未解問題是：當銀行、監理機關與企業可以在存款、穩定幣與代幣化資產之間選擇時，哪一種會先成為真正的「錢」？

title: Programmable Money: Turning Finance From a System That Records Transactions After the Fact Into One Where the Rules Are Embedded in the Money Itself
description: Stablecoins, tokenised deposits and programmable rails have moved from pilot to policy in 2026. Money itself can now carry instructions, conditions and compliance wherever it travels. This session traces what that shift means in practice for payments, capital markets and public finance, and the new skills institutions need to design and govern it. It also looks at how institutions are redesigning products, and teams, around value that enforces its own terms. The audience leaves with a working framework for where programmability creates genuine advantage and where it simply moves risk somewhere less visible. The underlying change is significant: rules that used to be enforced after the fact are now being written into the transaction before it ever happens, and by people whose roles look different than they did a year ago.
description_zh: 穩定幣、代幣化存款與可程式化支付軌道在 2026 年從試點走進政策。錢本身現在可以帶著指令、條件與法遵規則移動到任何地方。本場次追蹤這個轉變對支付、資本市場與公共財政的實際意義，以及機構需要哪些新技能來設計與治理它，同時檢視機構如何圍繞「會自我執行條款的價值」重新設計產品與團隊。聽眾將帶走一套可用的框架，判斷可程式化在哪裡創造真正的優勢，又在哪裡只是把風險搬到更不顯眼的地方。底層的變化相當重大：過去事後才執行的規則，如今在交易發生之前就被寫進去，而且動手寫的人，其角色與一年前已大不相同。

title: Agentic Infrastructure: 2027 Will Be the Year Agentic AI Touches Real Code, Real Money, Real Credit Decisions and Real Customers
description: Next year is set to be the point at which agentic AI starts touching real code, real money, real credit decisions and real customers. This is no longer confined to internal pilots. For CXOs, that changes the calculus: architecture and governance choices made now will shape competitive position for years. This opening session sets out why adoption, and the gap between leaders and laggards, are both accelerating at once. Attendees leave with a framing for the rest of the day's sessions on where the real risk and opportunity sit. One key question the discussion will dive into: how large a lead are the institutions getting agentic deployment right this year opening up over everyone still experimenting.
description_zh: 明年將是代理式 AI 開始觸及真實程式碼、真實資金、真實授信決策與真實客戶的轉折點，而這已經不再侷限於內部試點。對高階主管而言，這改變了整個算計：現在做下的架構與治理選擇，將形塑未來數年的競爭位置。這場開場說明為什麼採用速度、以及領先者與落後者之間的差距，正在同時加速。與會者將取得一個框架，用來理解當天後續場次所談的風險與機會究竟落在哪裡。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：今年把代理式部署做對的機構，究竟拉開了多大的領先幅度？

title: Programmable Money: Who Writes the Code the Financial System Runs On?
description: Money is acquiring software-like properties. It can now carry instructions, conditions and compliance logic wherever it moves, turning currency from a passive record of value into an active piece of code. Different regions are answering the question of control differently: the US leaning on banks and platforms, China centralising it through the state, and Europe building it into regulation from the outset. This discussion asks who ultimately gets to write that code, and whether these approaches converge or pull further apart. The audience leaves with a clearer view of where control over programmable money is likely to concentrate, region by region. One key question the discussion will dive into: if money becomes programmable, who actually decides the code it runs on, banks, platforms, or the state.
description_zh: 貨幣正在取得類似軟體的性質——它現在可以帶著指令、條件與法遵邏輯移動到任何地方，讓通貨從被動的價值紀錄，變成一段主動運行的程式碼。不同地區對「誰來控制」給出了不同答案：美國倚重銀行與平台，中國透過國家集中掌控，歐洲則從一開始就寫進法規。本場討論探問最終由誰來書寫這段程式碼，以及這些路徑會匯流還是漸行漸遠。聽眾將更清楚可程式化貨幣的控制權，在各地區可能集中到哪裡。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：如果錢變得可程式化，究竟誰來決定它運行的程式碼——銀行、平台，還是國家？

title: Tech Deep-Dive: Built to Bank: How Should FIs Rewire Their Organisations to Move Emerging Technologies From Experimentation to Enterprise-Wide Transformation?
description: Beneath the agentic headlines sits a technical layer that gets less attention: fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, or small, sovereign, on-premise models built to keep sensitive data in-house. For CXOs, this is where the real build-versus-buy decision actually gets made. This deep-dive works through how financial institutions should rewire for that layer, moving domain AI from experimentation to enterprise-wide transformation without losing data sovereignty. Attendees leave with sharper criteria for evaluating their own technical roadmap. One key question the discussion will dive into: does the build-versus-buy decision on domain AI lock in years of technical debt or advantage, with little room to reverse it later.
description_zh: 代理式 AI 的熱門話題底下，有一層較少被注意的技術選擇：微調、檢索增強生成（RAG），或是為了把敏感資料留在自家而打造的小型、主權、地端模型。對高階主管來說，真正的自建或外購決定就是在這一層做成的。本場深度對談梳理金融機構該如何為這一層重新佈線，讓領域 AI 從實驗走向全企業轉型，同時不失去資料主權。與會者將帶走更銳利的判準，用來評估自家的技術路線圖。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：領域 AI 的自建或外購決定，是不是會鎖定未來數年的技術債或技術優勢，而且日後幾乎沒有回頭的餘地？

title: Stablecoins: From Fringe to Framework
description: Stablecoins have moved out of the regulatory grey zone and into a proper legal framework. That shift changes the question facing every institution, from whether to engage at all to exactly how. Regulators in different markets are setting the terms at different speeds, and institutions no longer have the luxury of waiting for global consensus before deciding. This discussion works through the practical choices on the table: issuing, distributing or custodying stablecoins directly, against the risk of simply watching deposits drift toward whichever option moves fastest. Participants leave with a sharper sense of where their own institution sits on that spectrum, and what waiting actually costs under the new rules. One key question the discussion will dive into: whether to issue, distribute or custody stablecoins themselves, or simply watch deposits migrate to them regardless.
description_zh: 穩定幣已經走出監理灰色地帶，進入正式的法律框架。這個轉變改變了每一家機構要面對的問題——從「要不要參與」變成「究竟要怎麼參與」。各市場的監理機關訂定規則的速度不一，機構已經沒有餘裕等全球共識形成後再決定。本場討論梳理檯面上的實際選項：自行發行、負責分銷或直接提供託管，對照「眼睜睜看著存款流向動作最快的那一方」的風險。與會者將更清楚自家機構落在這個光譜的哪個位置，以及在新規則之下，等待的實際代價是什麼。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：該自己發行、分銷或託管穩定幣，還是無論如何都只能看著存款遷移過去？

title: Hiring for Programmable Money: Who's Building Teams in Stablecoins and Tokenization, and For What Roles?
description: Institutions are no longer asking whether to engage with stablecoins and tokenised assets, but how. That shift has created a hiring problem nobody fully priced in. This discussion maps which roles are actually being built inside banks, platforms and infrastructure providers to issue, distribute and custody programmable money. It also looks at where those skill sets are being sourced from. Attendees leave with a clearer picture of which roles are in genuine demand, and which ones are still being invented on the fly. One key question the discussion will dive into: is the talent to build programmable-money infrastructure even available at the scale institutions now need.
description_zh: 機構關心的已經不是要不要涉足穩定幣與代幣化資產，而是要怎麼做——而這個轉變製造出一個沒有人充分估算過的招募難題。本場討論盤點銀行、平台與基礎建設商為了發行、分銷與託管可程式化貨幣，實際上正在建立哪些職位，以及這些技能是從哪裡挖來的。與會者將更清楚哪些角色有真實需求，哪些又還在邊做邊定義。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：要打造可程式化貨幣的基礎建設，機構現在需要的人才規模，市場上真的供應得了嗎？

title: RWA & Tokenization: Do the Rules Follow The Asset or the Token?
description: Tokenised treasuries, funds and credit have grown fast enough that the wrapper technology is no longer the constraint. The open question is which set of rules actually travels with the asset once it is tokenised. Different jurisdictions are answering that question differently, and a token issued under one regime does not automatically carry the same protections when it moves across borders. This discussion works through where legal title, investor protections and jurisdictional rules sit once an asset exists as a token rather than a traditional instrument, and where that framework is still being written. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of the legal gaps that remain before tokenisation can scale past pilot volumes. One key question the discussion will dive into: as token wrappers move faster than the law, which rules actually travel with the asset once it changes hands.
description_zh: 代幣化的國庫券、基金與信貸成長夠快，快到包裝技術本身已不再是瓶頸；真正未解的問題是：資產一旦被代幣化，跟著它走的究竟是哪一套規則。不同司法管轄區的答案各異，而在某一法規之下發行的代幣，跨境之後並不會自動延續同樣的保障。本場討論梳理當資產以代幣、而非傳統工具的形式存在時，法律所有權、投資人保護與管轄規則各自落在哪裡，以及這套框架還有哪些部分仍在書寫中。聽眾將更清楚在代幣化能突破試點規模之前，還存在哪些法律缺口。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：當代幣包裝的演進速度快過法律，資產易手之後，究竟哪一套規則跟著走？

title: Building Compliance Into Code: The New Engineer-Regulator Hybrid Role
description: Compliance is starting to live inside code rather than around it. That shift is producing a role few institutions have a job description for yet. This discussion works through what compliance-as-code actually demands in practice. It needs engineers who understand regulatory intent, and regulators fluent enough in software to audit it. It also looks at who is currently closest to filling that gap. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of what to hire for and what to train internally instead. One key question the discussion will dive into: is compliance-as-code a job for engineers, for regulators, or for a role that does not exist yet.
description_zh: 法遵正開始住進程式碼裡面，而不是圍繞在它外面——這個轉變催生出一個少有機構寫得出職務說明的角色。本場討論梳理「法遵即程式碼」在實務上究竟要求什麼：它需要懂得監理意圖的工程師，也需要對軟體熟悉到足以稽核它的監理人員，同時檢視目前誰最接近填補這道缺口。聽眾將更清楚哪些該對外招募、哪些該在內部培養。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：法遵即程式碼是工程師的工作、監理人員的工作，還是一個目前還不存在的角色的工作？

title: If AI Strips Out the Cost, Who Captures the Value? Shareholders, Customers, or the Vendors Selling the Agents?
description: Cost is already coming out of financial-services functions like fraud review and customer service through agentic AI. This is happening well ahead of any consensus on who should benefit from the savings. For CXOs, that raises a strategic question as much as a technical one: pricing, vendor contracts and competitive positioning all shift depending on where that value lands. This discussion works through the mechanics of that value transfer, and where shareholders, customers and vendors are positioned to capture it. The audience leaves with a framework for thinking about their own pricing and vendor strategy as the savings materialise. One key question the discussion will dive into: if AI strips out most of the cost in a function, who actually captures that value, shareholders, customers, or the vendors selling the agents.
description_zh: 透過代理式 AI，詐欺審查與客戶服務等金融服務職能的成本已經在下降——而這遠遠早於任何關於「誰該享有這些節省」的共識。對高階主管來說，這既是技術問題也是策略問題：定價、供應商合約與競爭定位，都會隨著價值落點不同而改變。本場討論梳理這場價值轉移的運作機制，以及股東、客戶與供應商各自處在什麼位置去攫取它。聽眾將帶走一套框架，在節省逐步實現的過程中思考自家的定價與供應商策略。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：如果 AI 抽掉某個職能的大部分成本，這份價值究竟被誰拿走——股東、客戶，還是賣代理程式的供應商？

title: Can Regulation Be Written Into Money Itself? The Case for Rules in the Rails, Tokenized Deposits & Conditional Money
description: Tokenised deposits and conditional money take the programmability idea one layer deeper. They pilot whether settlement, eligibility and compliance can be embedded directly in the money rather than enforced around it. That raises a regulatory question few frameworks have caught up with: who is liable when the rule embedded in the transaction, not a human decision, turns out to be wrong. This discussion examines how the embedded-rules approach works in practice, and what it removes from the compliance function. It also looks at what new failure modes this introduces once the rule is baked into the transfer rather than checked afterwards. Attendees leave with a clearer view of where this model is genuinely ready, and where regulators are still working out how to hold it accountable. One key question the discussion will dive into: if compliance is embedded in the money itself, who is accountable when the embedded rule is wrong.
description_zh: 代幣化存款與條件式貨幣把可程式化的概念再往下推一層：它們試驗結算、資格與法遵能否直接嵌入貨幣本身，而不是在外圍執行。這帶出一個少有框架跟得上的監理問題——當出錯的是嵌在交易裡的規則、而非某個人的決定時，責任該由誰承擔。本場討論檢視這種「規則內嵌」的做法在實務上如何運作、它從法遵職能中拿掉了什麼，以及當規則被烤進轉帳本身、而不是事後查核時，會帶來哪些新的失效模式。與會者將更清楚這個模式在哪裡確實已經就緒，而監理機關又還在哪些地方摸索如何究責。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：如果法遵嵌在錢裡面，當那條內嵌的規則出錯時，該由誰負責？

title: AI is Redefining Headcount: Human-and-Agent Teams and the New Career Ladder
description: Inside the fastest-moving institutions, flatter hierarchies and human-and-agent teams are already becoming the norm. This is happening well ahead of any settled definition of what "headcount" even means once software sits inside the org chart. This discussion looks at how career ladders are being redrawn as agents absorb parts of entry-level and mid-tier work. It also looks at what that does to how people are hired, promoted and measured. Participants leave with a practical view of which structures are already working and which are still being improvised. The key question underneath it all: can career ladders and headcount definitions be redesigned before human-and-agent teams become the default rather than the exception.
description_zh: 在腳步最快的機構裡，扁平化的層級與人機協作團隊已逐漸成為常態——而這一切發生得遠早於「當軟體進入組織圖之後，人力編制到底是什麼」有任何定論。本場討論探討當代理程式吸收掉部分初階與中階工作時，職涯階梯如何被重新繪製，以及這對人員的招募、升遷與考核有什麼影響。與會者將務實看出哪些結構已經行得通、哪些還在且戰且走。底層的關鍵問題是：在人機協作團隊從例外變成預設之前，職涯階梯與人力編制的定義來得及重新設計嗎？

title: Programmable Money: Value Can Increasingly Carry Instructions, Conditions and Compliance Wherever It Moves
description: Tokenised deposits and purpose-bound money are being piloted from Singapore to Australia. These pilots are testing whether commercial-bank money can carry its own settlement, eligibility and compliance rules, rather than having them enforced around it afterwards. For CXOs, this is a build decision with long-term consequences: what to run at scale, and what stays a controlled pilot. This discussion looks at what that programmability layer actually requires under the hood, and how far institutions are from running it at scale. Attendees leave understanding the practical difference between value that follows rules and value that is simply monitored. One key question the discussion will dive into: does programmable money increase trust, or does it just create a new kind of control over economic activity.
description_zh: 從新加坡到澳洲，代幣化存款與限定用途貨幣正在進行試點，測試商業銀行貨幣能否自行帶著結算、資格與法遵規則，而不是事後在外圍執行。對高階主管而言，這是一個影響深遠的建置決定：什麼該大規模上線，什麼該留在受控試點。本場討論探討這層可程式化在底層究竟需要什麼，以及機構距離大規模運行還有多遠。與會者將理解「會遵循規則的價值」與「只是被監控的價值」，實務上差別何在。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：可程式化貨幣是提升了信任，還是只是創造出一種對經濟活動的新控制手段？

title: What It Will Take to Move Cross-Border Tokenization From Proof-of-Concept to Production, Including Settlement Layers, Legal Frameworks and Interoperable Standards
description: Cross-border tokenisation has proven itself in pilots. Production requires settlement layers, legal frameworks and interoperable standards that no single jurisdiction can build alone. That raises a sequencing question: which markets to prioritise, and which standards to build toward before the rules fully settle. This discussion maps what is actually missing between proof-of-concept and live cross-border deployment, and which institutions and regulators are closest to closing the gap. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of the sequencing required before tokenised assets can move across borders as routinely as payments do today. One key question the discussion will dive into: is cross-border tokenisation stalled by the technology, or by which jurisdiction is willing to move first.
description_zh: 跨境代幣化已在試點階段證明可行，但要進入量產，需要結算層、法律框架與可互通標準——而這些沒有任何單一司法管轄區能獨力建成。這帶出一個先後次序的問題：該優先耕耘哪些市場，又該在規則完全底定之前，朝哪些標準靠攏。本場討論盤點從概念驗證到實際跨境上線之間究竟還缺什麼，以及哪些機構與監理機關最接近補上這道缺口。聽眾將更清楚在代幣化資產能像今日支付一樣稀鬆平常地跨境流動之前，需要什麼樣的推進順序。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：跨境代幣化卡住的原因是技術，還是「哪個司法管轄區願意先動」？

title: Built to Bank: Who Builds the Bank's Own LLM? The talent Race Behind Domain AI
description: The build-versus-buy decision on domain AI made this year will shape everything built on top of it for years. Yet few institutions have the specialist bench to make that call with confidence. This discussion gets into who has the skills to build a bank's own large language model in-house. It also looks at where that expertise is currently concentrated, and where it needs to spread. Attendees leave knowing what a credible in-house AI team actually looks like today. The underlying pressure: the domain-AI talent race is moving faster than most institutions' hiring and build decisions can keep up with.
description_zh: 今年做下的領域 AI 自建或外購決定，將形塑其上數年間建造的一切——但少有機構具備足夠的專才陣容，能有把握地做出這個判斷。本場討論深入探討：誰有能力在自家內部打造銀行專屬的大型語言模型，這些專業目前又集中在哪裡、需要往哪裡擴散。與會者將了解今天一支可信的自建 AI 團隊實際上長什麼樣子。底層的壓力在於：領域 AI 的人才競賽，跑得比多數機構的招募與建置決策還快。

title: Programmable Money: The Implications Reach Past Payments Into Trade, Capital Markets, Public Finance and Economic Policy
description: Programmable money was designed to solve a payments problem. But the same properties, conditions, instructions and compliance logic attached to value, apply just as well to tax collection, subsidy distribution and public finance. Once policymakers start treating it as general-purpose infrastructure rather than a payments feature, the questions shift from technical to political: who sets the conditions, and whose policy priorities get written into the code. This short discussion frames how far the implications of programmable money actually reach, and sets up the broader economic-policy conversation for the sessions that follow. One key question the discussion will dive into: could programmable money end up redefining taxation, subsidies and cross-border commerce, not just payments.
description_zh: 可程式化貨幣原本是為了解決支付問題而設計的，但同樣的性質——附著在價值上的條件、指令與法遵邏輯——也同樣適用於稅收、補貼發放與公共財政。一旦政策制定者開始把它視為通用基礎建設、而非一項支付功能，問題就會從技術轉向政治：由誰設定條件，以及誰的政策優先順序被寫進程式碼。這場簡短討論勾勒可程式化貨幣的影響實際延伸到多遠，並為後續場次更廣泛的經濟政策對談鋪路。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：可程式化貨幣最終會不會重新定義的不只是支付，還包括課稅、補貼與跨境商務？

title: Will Regulation Increasingly Be Enforced Through Software Rather Than Supervision, and What Happens When the Code Is Wrong?
description: Regulators have traditionally supervised financial activity after the fact, through reporting, audits and inspections. Programmable money changes that: it makes it possible to enforce a rule the moment a transaction is attempted, rather than checking it afterwards. That shift moves power away from supervisors and toward whoever writes the rule into the code in the first place. This discussion explores what that means for regulators, institutions and the people writing those rules, and what embedded enforcement demands of governance as a result. Participants leave with a sharper sense of where software-enforced compliance is heading. One key question the discussion will dive into: will regulation increasingly be enforced through software rather than supervision, and what happens when the code is wrong.
description_zh: 監理機關傳統上是透過申報、稽核與檢查，事後監督金融活動。可程式化貨幣改變了這一點：它讓規則可以在交易被發動的當下就強制執行，而不是事後查核。這個轉變把權力從監督者手中，移向最初把規則寫進程式碼的人。本場討論探討這對監理機關、機構，以及書寫這些規則的人意味著什麼，以及內嵌式執法因此對治理提出了什麼要求。與會者將更清楚由軟體執行的法遵正走向何方。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：監理會不會愈來愈透過軟體、而非監督來執行？而當程式碼寫錯時，會發生什麼事？

title: When Deposits, Stablecoins and Tokenized Assets All Compete as "Money", Which One Wins the Balance Sheet, and Whose Balance Sheet Does It Sit On?
What New Institutions Will Emerge to Certify Authenticity in Digital Finance?
description: Trust is becoming the scarcest resource in finance. AI-generated identities, synthetic data and manufactured evidence are multiplying faster than the tools built to catch them. This discussion examines what it actually takes to make identity, transactions and provenance verifiable by design, rather than assumed on trust. It also looks at who is best placed to stand behind that verification, at a moment when no single jurisdiction can set that standard alone. Attendees leave with a view of where new certifying bodies are likely to emerge, and which existing institutions, national or international, are best placed to take on that role instead. One key question the discussion will dive into: what new institutions will emerge to certify authenticity in digital finance, and who gets to decide.
description_zh: 信任正成為金融業最稀缺的資源。AI 生成的身分、合成資料與偽造證據，增生的速度快過用來揪出它們的工具。本場討論檢視要讓身分、交易與來源「從設計上就可驗證」、而不是預設可信，實際需要什麼，並探討在沒有任何單一司法管轄區能獨力訂定標準的此刻，誰最適合為這份驗證背書。與會者將了解新的認證機構可能從哪裡冒出來，又有哪些既有的國內或國際組織更適合承接這個角色。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：數位金融的真偽認證會出現什麼樣的新機構，而由誰來決定？

title: PolyFinTech100 API Hackathon
description: Automation and AI are redefining which roles an economy needs. This is happening at the exact moment education and training systems are struggling to keep pace. Governments are left managing rising unemployment and widening skills shortages at the same time. This discussion looks at what reskilling and job redesign need to look like to keep an entire generation inside the workforce rather than locked out of it. It leaves the audience with concrete examples of where public-private reskilling models are actually working. One key question the discussion will dive into: can reskilling keep pace with automation, or will a generation of entry-level roles disappear before it does.
description_zh: 自動化與 AI 正在重新定義一個經濟體需要哪些職位，而這恰好發生在教育與訓練體系難以跟上的時刻，政府因此得同時應付攀升的失業率與擴大的技能缺口。本場討論探討再培訓與職務再設計該長什麼樣子，才能把整個世代留在勞動市場內、而不是被排除在外，並提供公私協力再培訓模式真正見效的具體案例。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：再培訓跟得上自動化嗎？還是一整個世代的初階職位會先消失？

title: Digital Public Infrastructure: Framing the Ownership Debate
description: Payment rails, identity systems and data-exchange infrastructure used to sit inside proprietary platforms. Increasingly, they are being built and run as open, shared public goods instead. That shift raises a policy question with no settled answer yet: who is accountable for infrastructure nobody owns outright. This short discussion frames the resulting ownership debate: whether treating core financial infrastructure as open source genuinely builds resilience, or simply moves systemic risk somewhere harder to see and govern. It sets the terms for the fuller debate on ownership that follows. One key question the discussion will dive into: does treating infrastructure as open source build resilience, or does it just move the systemic risk somewhere less visible.
description_zh: 支付軌道、身分系統與資料交換基礎建設過去多半座落在專有平台之內，如今卻愈來愈常以開放共享的公共財形式建置與營運。這個轉變帶出一個尚無定論的政策問題：沒有人完全擁有的基礎建設，該由誰負責。這場簡短討論勾勒隨之而來的所有權辯論：把核心金融基礎建設當成開源，究竟是真的強化了韌性，還是只是把系統性風險搬到更難看見、更難治理的地方。它為後續更完整的所有權辯論定調。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：把基礎建設當成開源會建立韌性，還是只是把系統性風險移到更不顯眼的地方？

title: Open Source and Digital Public Infrastructure
description: Some of the most important financial infrastructure now under discussion may end up as a public good rather than a proprietary platform. That reshapes decades of assumptions about ownership and competition. For policymakers, this raises a question with no settled precedent: who is accountable for infrastructure that no single institution owns. This short opening frames why open-source and digital public infrastructure are moving up the agenda, setting up the deeper conversation that follows. Attendees leave with a working sense of what is actually at stake in the ownership question. One key question the discussion will dive into: is competitive advantage shifting from owning infrastructure to building on top of shared infrastructure someone else controls.
description_zh: 目前討論中最重要的一些金融基礎建設，最終可能會成為公共財、而非專有平台，這將重塑數十年來關於所有權與競爭的假設。對政策制定者而言，這帶出一個沒有成例可循的問題：沒有任何單一機構擁有的基礎建設，該由誰負責。這場簡短開場說明為什麼開源與數位公共基礎建設在議程上的位置不斷上升，為後續更深入的對談鋪路。與會者將實際掌握所有權問題的核心利害所在。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：競爭優勢是否正從「擁有基礎建設」轉向「在別人掌控的共享基礎建設之上建造」？

title: Can Digital Public Infrastructure Become a New Form of Economic Diplomacy?
description: Digital public infrastructure built for payments and identity at national scale is starting to cross borders. That shift turns technical rails into a tool of statecraft, rather than domestic delivery alone. For policymakers, this raises questions that go beyond interoperability: whose standards travel, and what obligations come attached when infrastructure crosses a border. This discussion examines how governments are using shared infrastructure to extend influence and build cooperation beyond their own borders, and what that means for institutions operating across those corridors. Attendees leave with a sharper read on which infrastructure partnerships carry geopolitical weight, not just technical convenience. One key question the discussion will dive into: can digital public infrastructure become a new form of economic diplomacy.
description_zh: 為全國規模的支付與身分而建的數位公共基礎建設，開始跨出國界，讓技術軌道從單純的境內服務，變成一種治國工具。對政策制定者而言，這帶出超越互通性的問題：誰的標準得以流通，以及基礎建設跨越國界時附帶了什麼義務。本場討論檢視各國政府如何運用共享基礎建設，把影響力與合作延伸到自身疆界之外，以及這對在這些走廊上營運的機構意味著什麼。與會者將更敏銳地判斷，哪些基礎建設夥伴關係帶有地緣政治份量，而不只是技術上的便利。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：數位公共基礎建設能不能成為一種新形態的經濟外交？

title: Should Critical Financial Infrastructure Belong to Markets, Governments, or Communities?
description: Digital public infrastructure is forcing a genuine rethink of who should own the rails that a country's payments, identity and data exchange run on. For decades, ownership was assumed to sit naturally with the private sector or the state. That assumption is now breaking down as the underlying technology itself changes what ownership can look like, from centralised systems to distributed, community-governed models. This discussion debates the alternative models on the table, from government-run utilities to community-governed commons, and what each implies for competition, investment and accountability. The audience leaves with a clearer view of which ownership model actually fits their own market's stage of development. One key question the discussion will dive into: should critical financial infrastructure belong to markets, governments, or communities.
description_zh: 數位公共基礎建設正迫使各界真正重新思考：一個國家的支付、身分與資料交換所依賴的軌道，究竟該由誰擁有。數十年來，所有權被理所當然地認為屬於民間部門或國家，而隨著底層技術本身改變了所有權的可能樣貌——從中心化系統到分散式、社群治理的模式——這個假設正在瓦解。本場討論辯論檯面上的各種替代模式，從政府經營的公用事業到社群治理的公共財，以及每一種對競爭、投資與問責分別意味著什麼。聽眾將更清楚哪一種所有權模式，真正契合自己市場的發展階段。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：關鍵金融基礎建設該屬於市場、政府，還是社群？

title: Layers of Trust: Can Trust Become Programmable?
description: As AI-generated identities and synthetic data spread across financial services, trust itself is becoming the scarcest resource. Assumed authenticity is no longer a safe default for institutions or their customers. For policymakers, this raises a question no existing framework fully answers: who has the authority to certify what is real. This discussion looks at technologies that make identity, transactions and provenance verifiable by design, and at what new institutions might need to exist purely to certify that authenticity. The audience leaves with a clearer sense of where verification, not speed or intelligence, is becoming the real competitive edge. One key question the discussion will dive into: can trust become programmable.
description_zh: 隨著 AI 生成的身分與合成資料在金融服務業擴散，信任本身正成為最稀缺的資源；對機構與其客戶而言，「預設為真」已不再是安全的起點。對政策制定者來說，這帶出一個現有框架都無法完整回答的問題：誰有權認證什麼是真的。本場討論探討讓身分、交易與來源在設計上就可驗證的技術，以及可能需要有哪些新機構，單純為了認證這份真實性而存在。聽眾將更清楚真正的競爭優勢正轉向「驗證能力」，而不是速度或智慧。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：信任能不能被程式化？

title: Agentic Commerce: Identity, Mandate, Micro-Transactions
description: The infrastructure for AI-initiated payments is already live: signed proof of intent, one-time credentials, machine-to-machine micropayments. This is well ahead of the trust needed for people to actually rely on it. The underlying technology has moved faster than the systems built to verify who, or what, is actually authorising a payment. This discussion examines the identity and mandate questions that come with letting an agent spend on someone's behalf, and where the data trail ends up. Attendees leave with a sharper view of the gap between what agentic commerce can already do and what still needs trust before it scales. One key question the discussion will dive into: as agentic commerce leaves a richer data trail, who owns that data exhaust, the bank, the platform, or the customer.
description_zh: AI 發動支付的基礎建設已經上線：帶簽章的意圖證明、一次性憑證、機器對機器的微支付——而這遠遠跑在「人們真的願意依賴它」所需的信任之前。底層技術的演進速度，快過用來驗證「究竟是誰、或什麼在授權這筆支付」的系統。本場討論檢視讓代理程式代人花錢所衍生的身分與授權問題，以及資料軌跡最後流向何處。與會者將更清楚代理式商務「已經做得到的事」與「規模化之前仍需建立的信任」之間，落差有多大。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：當代理式商務留下愈來愈豐富的資料軌跡，這些資料排放物歸誰所有——銀行、平台，還是客戶？

title: The Last Generation of Jobs?
description:
Automation is changing which jobs an economy needs, faster than education and training systems can keep up, leaving governments to face rising unemployment and skills shortages together. This discussion looks at what reskilling and job redesign need to look like to keep young workers in the workforce, pointing to public-private models that are already working. Attendees leave with a clearer read on how to hold a generation inside the workforce.
The key question the discussion looks to answer: can reskilling keep pace with automation, or does a generation of entry-level jobs disappear first?
description_zh:
自動化正在改變一個經濟體需要哪些工作，而速度快過教育與訓練體系所能跟上，政府因此得同時面對攀升的失業率與技能短缺。本場討論探討再培訓與職務再設計該長什麼樣子，才能把年輕工作者留在勞動市場內，並指出已經見效的公私協力模式。與會者將更清楚該如何把一個世代留在勞動市場裡。
討論想回答的關鍵問題：再培訓跟得上自動化嗎？還是一整個世代的初階工作會先消失？

title: The Capital Rewiring: Great Capital Reallocation - The Breakages, the Flows and Deployment
description: Capital no longer moves evenly, it's repricing and clustering hard around AI, energy transition, and a handful of high-growth emerging markets. This keynote traces where that reallocation is actually landing and what it takes to be investment-ready enough to capture it. Attendees leave with a sharper read on which sectors and regions are pulling capital away from its old defaults. The key question it looks to answer: can institutions reorganise as fast as capital is moving, or does timing become the real bottleneck?
description_zh: 資本不再均勻流動——它正在重新定價，並向 AI、能源轉型以及少數幾個高成長新興市場強力聚集。這場主題演講追蹤這場資本重新配置實際落到了哪裡，以及要「夠格接住它」需要什麼樣的投資準備度。與會者將更敏銳地判斷，哪些產業與地區正把資本從過去的預設去處拉走。它想回答的關鍵問題是：機構重組的速度，跟得上資本移動的速度嗎？還是時機本身才是真正的瓶頸？

title: The Evolution of the Investor Thesis: Regional Perspectives and Opening Up Access to Capital
description: Investment theses are being rebuilt from scratch, not just tweaked at the edges. What counts as credible is shifting fastest toward AI, energy transition, and high-growth emerging markets, pushing allocators and founders to question assumptions they've relied on for years. The discussion works through how access to capital is opening up, or staying closed, depending on geography and sector. Attendees leave better placed to read where their own strategy sits against where capital is actually moving. The key question it looks to answer: whose thesis shifts first when capital reprices, the allocator's or the founder's?
description_zh: 投資論述正在從頭重建，而不只是邊緣微調。什麼算是可信的標的，正最快速地向 AI、能源轉型與高成長新興市場傾斜，逼得資產配置者與創業者重新檢視他們倚賴多年的假設。本場討論梳理取得資本的門檻正在如何打開、或依然緊閉——端看地理位置與產業別。與會者將更有能力判斷自身策略，相對於資本真正的流向處在什麼位置。它想回答的關鍵問題是：當資本重新定價時，誰的論述會先改變——配置者的，還是創業者的？

title: Driving New Sources of Growth and Reinventing Operating Models
description: Landing capital is one thing, actually reshaping the business to use it is another. Institutions chasing new sources of growth are finding that where capital lands matters less than whether the operating model underneath can absorb it. This founders panel tests whether operating-model change reflects a genuine growth strategy or defensive necessity dressed up as one. Attendees leave with a clearer set of questions to ask before backing any transformation plan pitched as growth. The key question it looks to answer: is reinventing the operating model actually a growth strategy, or a defensive one dressed up as growth?
description_zh: 拿到資本是一回事，真正重塑事業去運用它又是另一回事。追逐新成長來源的機構發現，資本落在哪裡，遠不如底下的營運模式能不能吸收它來得重要。這場創業者座談檢驗營運模式的改變，究竟反映的是真正的成長策略，還是包裝成成長的防禦性必要之舉。與會者將帶走一組更清楚的提問，在支持任何打著成長旗號的轉型計畫之前先問過一遍。它想回答的關鍵問題是：重塑營運模式真的是成長策略，還是披著成長外衣的防禦策略？

title: The Policy Rewiring: Navigating a World Fortresses - Key Tensions Points and Areas for Harmonisation
description: Technology moves globally, regulation still stops at the border. Regulators face a widening challenge, enabling innovation while safeguarding stability across jurisdictions never built to align. This keynote maps the sharpest tensions in AI, digital-asset, and open-finance regulation, and where harmonisation is realistic versus wishful. The key question it looks to answer: is regulatory fragmentation a temporary lag, or the new permanent shape of the system?
description_zh: 技術在全球流動，監理卻仍止步於國界。監理機關面對日益擴大的難題：在一套從未為彼此對齊而設計的跨司法管轄體系中，既要促成創新、又要守住穩定。這場主題演講盤點 AI、數位資產與開放金融監理上最尖銳的張力，以及哪些協調是務實可行的、哪些只是一廂情願。它想回答的關鍵問題是：監理分歧是暫時的落差，還是這個體系未來永久的樣貌？

title: The Great Coordination: Managing Regulatory Multiplicity
description: Policy rewiring is about who moves fastest inside the gaps between rules. Regulatory strategy is now a competitive advantage, not just a compliance requirement, as sandboxes and new frameworks spread unevenly. This panel looks at how institutions manage that multiplicity, from cross-border cooperation to interoperable supervision. The key question it looks to answer: can regimes never designed to talk to each other coordinate fast enough to keep up with innovation?
description_zh: 政策重塑的重點在於：誰能在規則的縫隙之間動得最快。隨著沙盒與新框架不均勻地擴散，監理策略如今是一種競爭優勢，而不只是法遵要求。本場座談探討機構如何應對這種多重性，從跨境合作到可互通的監督機制。它想回答的關鍵問題是：一套從未被設計成能彼此對話的監理體制，協調的速度跟得上創新嗎？

title: The Race to Real-Time: C-suite Dialogue on Instant Payments
description: Payments infrastructure is being rewired in parallel, with no single rail yet winning the race to become the default. Several real-time payment protocols are live across markets, and none has pulled decisively ahead, leaving institutions to build strategy without knowing which will win. This CEO dialogue works through what it takes to make instant payments interoperable across borders, from messaging standards to settlement, without betting on a single winner. The key question it looks to answer: do institutions bet on one rail, or build for a permanently fragmented world?
description_zh: 支付基礎建設正在同步重新佈線，而目前還沒有任何一條軌道贏得「成為預設」的競賽。多套即時支付協定已在各市場上線，沒有一個決定性地領先，機構因此得在不知道誰會勝出的情況下擬定策略。這場執行長對談梳理要讓即時支付跨境互通需要什麼——從訊息標準到結算——同時不押注在單一贏家身上。它想回答的關鍵問題是：機構該押注單一軌道，還是為一個永久分裂的世界做準備？
